$comment: seam-sdk's EXTENDED integer cases for RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization.
Machine-emitted by scripts/emit_jcs_int_vectors.py -- no digest here was typed by hand.
with seam-runtime and is not edited from this repo; this file is a superset for a trap
CONTRACT: an implementation MUST emit `canonical` byte-for-byte for every case that has
it, and MUST refuse every case marked `rejected` -- refusing an accepted case or
accepting a rejected one is equally a break. `digest` is tool_input_digest over the
`int` is a STRING because parsing it as a JSON number loses precision in JavaScript
before any implementation could be tested.
WHY: JCS numbers are IEEE doubles, so the only integers that can appear in canonical
output are those ES6 Number::toString prints as themselves. 'Exactly representable as a
double' is a DIFFERENT and wrong rule: 2**60 is representable and renders as
1152921504606847000. The two rules agree on every power of ten, so eight of the cases
below are machine-searched rather than chosen -- four accepted, four refused, drawn at
random from the interval where the two candidate rules disagree.

cases.name: zero
cases.why: the degenerate case, and -0 must not appear

cases.name: one
cases.why: a plain small integer takes the unchanged fast path

cases.name: negative-one
cases.why: sign handling on the fast path

cases.name: max-safe
cases.why: the 2^53 boundary is INCLUSIVE — the old rule tested >, not >=

cases.name: negative-max-safe
cases.why: the boundary is symmetric

cases.name: max-safe-plus-one
cases.why: rounds to 2^53; not representable at all
cases.reason: integer 9007199254740993 is not JCS-renderable as itself: canonicalizing it would emit 9007199254740992, a different value. JSON numbers are IEEE doubles; this integer is not one a double prints back unchanged, so digesting it would sign a value nobody supplied.

cases.name: max-safe-plus-two
cases.why: the first integer above the boundary that IS renderable

cases.name: ten-to-16
cases.why: the case reported in seam-sdk#60: accepted as 1e16, refused as an int

cases.name: negative-ten-to-16
cases.why: the reported case, negated

cases.name: ten-to-20
cases.why: largest decade ES6 still prints without an exponent

cases.name: two-to-55
cases.why: EXACTLY REPRESENTABLE and still refused — ES6 shortens it
cases.reason: integer 36028797018963968 is not JCS-renderable as itself: canonicalizing it would emit 36028797018963970, a different value. JSON numbers are IEEE doubles; this integer is not one a double prints back unchanged, so digesting it would sign a value nobody supplied.
